title: Chunking and Embedding Documents
description: Implement document ingestion, text splitting, and embedding generation in C# using popular .NET libraries.

blocks.text: Chunking determines whether retrieval can find the right passage. Embeddings determine whether that passage can be found by meaning. In this lesson, you implement both stages using provider-agnostic C# code.

blocks.title: Common strategies
items: **Fixed-size chunks** — simple and predictable; may cut sentences or tables badly.
**Sentence or paragraph chunks** — respects natural boundaries but varies in size.
**Recursive character splitting** — breaks large chunks into smaller ones while preserving structure.
**Document-aware splitting** — honors Markdown headings, HTML tags, or PDF sections.

blocks.text: Prefer an abstraction layer over direct HTTP calls. Microsoft.Extensions.AI provides IEmbeddingGenerator, which lets you swap OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, or local providers without changing business logic.

blocks.title: Measure chunk quality
blocks.text: Before embedding thousands of documents, manually inspect fifty chunks. Fix chunking rules before you invest in embedding and indexing.

blocks.title: Build a Chunking Pipeline
blocks.description: Ingest a Markdown or JSON document collection and split it into chunks with metadata.
steps: Create a console app or ASP.NET Core worker.
Read a few Markdown files from a folder.
Split them into chunks with title and section metadata.
Log chunk counts and average chunk length.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You should have working chunking code and evidence that your metadata preserves document structure.
